author: Peter Vercoe
description: The United Arab Emirates closed its airspace early Tuesday morning, further setting back the region’s efforts to restore regular flight operations as the Iran conflict extends into a third week.
title: UAE Closes Airspace as Precautionary Measure, WAM Reports

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Maggie Goodlander of New Hampshire calls on President Donald Trump to provide a “basic rationale” for the war in Iran as additional US troops deploy to the region. Heather Conley, Nonresident Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute, says President Trump was correct to delay a planned summit with China’s Xi Jinping, noting the optics would be “terrible” if the president visited China as the Iran war intensifies. Finland’s President Alexander Stubb said NATO allies have to take Donald Trump at his word when the US president puts the future of the alliance on the line to safeguard passage through the Strait of Hormuz. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump: US Requests Delay of Xi Summit Amid War | Balance of Power: Late Edition 03/16/2026

description: Heather Conley, Nonresident Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute and Former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for the Bureau of European and Eurasian Affairs, says President Trump was correct to delay a planned summit with China’s Xi Jinping, noting the optics would be “terrible” if the president visited China as the Iran war intensifies. She also says the administration failed to lay diplomatic groundwork with allies before the invasion, making it harder to now rally support to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz. She speaks on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump ‘Correct’ to Delay Xi Meeting: Heather Conley

description: Rep. Maggie Goodlander of New Hampshire calls on President Donald Trump to provide a “basic rationale” for the war in Iran as additional US troops deploy to the region. She also weighs in on efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Trump’s comments about the “honor” of taking over Cuba and the ongoing DHS shutdown. She speaks on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. Goodlander: ‘This Is No Way to Run a War’

description: President Donald Trump says he had requested China delay a summit with Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping for about a month, citing the need to oversee the Iran war. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says He Requested 'Month or So' Delay to Xi Summit

description: When asked in the Oval Office if the war could end this week, President Donald Trump says “I don’t think so, but it’ll be soon.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says Iran War Will End Soon, Not This Week

description: President Donald Trump signed an executive order to launch an task force targeting federal benefits fraud to be led by Vice President JD Vance, intensifying the administration’s oversight of federal funds in Democratic-led states.
title: Trump Signs Order to Launch Vance-Led Anti-Fraud Task Force

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump said he had requested China delay a summit with Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping for about a month, saying it was important for him to remain in Washington to oversee the Iran war.
title: Trump Says He Asked China to Delay Xi Summit Due to Iran War

description: Finland’s President Alexander Stubb says NATO allies have to take President Donald Trump at his word when it comes to trying to secure the Strait of Hormuz. “We obviously have to take everything that the president of the United States says seriously,” Stubb told Bloomberg's Francine Lacqua. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Finland's Stubb Says NATO Should Take Trump Seriously

description: Finland’s President Alexander Stubb said NATO allies have to take Donald Trump at his word when the US president puts the future of the alliance on the line to safeguard passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

description: Trump has allies and foes guessing about his endgame.

description: Puneet Talwar, senior advisor at Albright Stonebridge Group and former US ambassador to Morocco, talks about what President Donald Trump's options are now in Iran. He speaks on Bloomberg The Close. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: What Are Trump's Options in Iran?

description: The massive Shah natural gas field in the United Arab Emirates caught fire after a drone strike.

title: RFK Jr.'s Changes to Vaccine Schedule, Panel Paused by Judge

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec speak with Bloomberg Opinion international affairs columnist on President Trump's demands that allies back US efforts to protect tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and why some countries may want to use their assistance as leverage. Then, Alberto Gallo, CIO of Andromeda Capital Management, on the private credit landscape as investment in AI increases private credit funds' exposure to hyperscalers. Plus, Ed Ludlow breaks down what to expect from Nvidia's GTC conference - the super bowl of AI conferences - as the company tries to jumpstart the idling stock. Then, Racquel Oden, US head of international wealth and private banking at HSBC, talks market landscape as Wall Street tries to parse what's next in the war with Iran. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Asks Allies For Help With Hormuz, Nvidia GTC Underway | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/16/2026

author: Jorge Valero, Alberto Nardelli
description: The European Union said it’s close to finalizing a trade deal with Australia after years of negotiations.
title: EU Says It’s Nearing a Free-Trade Agreement With Australia

author: Eric Martin
description: Cuba is moving to allow more investment from Cubans living abroad as part of a larger effort to bolster the state-dominated economy amid increased pressure from the US, one of the country’s top diplomats said.
title: Cuban Envoy Says Island Will Be Open to More Exile Investment

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Kailey Leinz discusses the latest from the Middle East. On today's show, Chatham House Associate Fellow Natasha Hall, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Airlines for America President and CEO Chris Sununu. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Appeals for Help With Hormuz | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/16/2026

description: President Donald Trump has long complained about what he sees as unfair treatment from the major television networks. Now he’s employing a new enforcer in the fight: the Federal Communications Commission.

title: Chile’s Kast Races to Harden Border, Cut Tax, Slash Red Tape

description: Mine-clearing drones like those touted by UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer as a possible way to ease Iran’s grip on shipping have serious limitations that prevent them from materially changing the situation in the Strait of Hormuz.

description: Cuba’s electric grid suffered a total power failure Monday as the island nation struggles with fuel supplies amid a de facto US oil blockade to pressure the communist government.

description: Wilbur Ross, former US Secretary of Commerce and chairman, president, and CEO of Ross Acquisition Corp II, joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Markets." They discuss the Iran War's impact on oil prices and affordability.  (Source: Bloomberg)

description: Shipments surged by the most in more than a year as crude flooded out of Russia’s Pacific and Arctic ports

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump reiterated his appeals for help from other nations to secure the Strait of Hormuz, saying that Iran was nearly obliterated even as the war keeps roiling oil markets and global shipping.

description: The US Department of Justice has proposed changes that would make it easier for states to win a fast-track federal review of death penalty cases as part of President Donald Trump’s push to ramp up capital punishment.
title: DOJ Plans to Lower Bar for States to Fast-Track Executions

description: White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles has been diagnosed with early stage breast cancer but plans to continue working, President Donald Trump said Monday.
title: Trump Says Wiles Has Cancer, Will Continue as Chief of Staff

author: Peter Martin, Alex Wickham, Josh Xiao
description: After years of being antagonized by President Donald Trump, US allies in Europe and Asia are in no hurry to bow to his demand that they send ships into a war he started — and has claimed to have won already.

description: Ireland sits at the center of US tech, pharma and investment flows into Europe. So how are geopolitical tensions, tariffs and AI investment shaping that relationship? Peter Burke, Ireland's Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment joined Bloomberg Open Interest with insight. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Ireland's Economy & US Ties

description: Geopolitics, market volatility, and the rise of AI are all colliding with shareholder activism this year. What it means for proxy fights, dealmaking, and the pressure on corporate boards is coming into focus.  Kai Liekefett, Co-Chair of Shareholder Activism Practice at Sidley joined Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about why activists may be holding back and what's building beneath the surface. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Proxy Fight Season Faces Geopolitical Headwinds

description: A tense exchange on the cost of the Iran conflict. Bloomberg Open Interest presses House Ways & Means Chair Jason Smith on rising gas prices, war spending, and what short-term military action actually means. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. Jason Smith Defends Iran War Strategy

description: Tina Fordham, the Founder and Geopolitical Strategist of Fordham Global Foresight joined Bloomberg Open Interest with a geopolitical warning. She says expectations for a short conflict with Iran are  a “fat chance.” She argues rising oil prices and eased sanctions could actually boost Russia and Iran, while the White House still hasn’t clearly defined its endgame. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Geopolitical Risks From Iran War Grow

author: Selcan Hacaoglu, Andrea Palasciano

description: The British Broadcasting Corp. asked a judge to toss out President Donald Trump’s $10 billion lawsuit over a misleading edit of his speech before the Jan. 6, 2021 assault on the Capitol, arguing the lawsuit will chill free speech and undermine “robust reporting.”
title: BBC Asks Judge to Dismiss Trump $10 Billion Defamation Suit

description:
The war in Ukraine has already put a dent in American missile stockpiles. And now the war in Iran is further depleting supply.

On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast, Tom Karako, director of the Missile Defense Project at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, joins Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway to discuss the role missile defense plays in warfare. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: War in Iran Is Chewing Through American Missile Stockpiles

description: The FAA has barred all flights over Mar-a-Lago below 2,000 feet, even when the US president isn’t at his beach club.

description: US President Donald Trump is weakening the international order by waging war on Iran, according to Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.
title: Spain’s Sánchez Says Trump’s War on Iran Undermines Global Order

description: David Seif of Nomura Securities International says he doesn't think Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell will stay on until the end of his term in 2028, but he could stick around just long enough complicate succession plans for President Donald Trump. Seif speaks on Bloomberg Surveillance. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Powell Could Stay on Fed Long Enough to Complicate Things for Trump, Seif Says

This will be the first time we hear from Chair Jerome Powell since the US-Israel war with Iran started. Bloomberg's Enda Curran reports.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fed Expected to Hold Rates Steady Due to War, Energy Shock

description: Bloomberg Opinion columnist, Adrian Wooldridge, discusses his new book 'Centrists of the World Unite! The Lost Genius of Liberalism'. He argues the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence comes at a worrying moment in American history, with fundamental liberal principles under attack from illiberal forces on both the right and the left. The US, argues Wooldridge, should renew its faith in its founding liberal principles to tackle the challenges ahead. He was speaking on Bloomberg's The Pulse with Francine Lacqua. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: How The US Gave Up On Liberalism: Bloomberg Opinion's Wooldridge

description: US President Donald Trump’s demand for China to send warships to the Strait of Hormuz will almost certainly be rejected out of hand. description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

On today's show, US President Donald Trump has demanded other countries help secure passage for ships in the Strait of Hormuz as Iran continues to disrupt the region’s energy markets.

Trump told the FT his planned summit with Xi Jinping may be delayed if China doesn’t assist in unblocking Hormuz.

Dubai said flights are gradually resuming at its main airport after a temporary suspension following a nearby drone strike.

Today's guests: Pilar Gomez-Bravo, Co-CIO for Fixed Income at MFS Investment Management. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran War: Trump Hormuz Plea & Trump-Xi Summit Possible Delay: FT | Daybreak Europe 3/16/2026

description: The key port of Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates was hit again on Monday. The damage from the latest strike was being assessed, people familiar with the matter said. The site is the only outlet for the country that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz and oil loading at the port had restarted over the weekend after a drone strike caused a fire on Saturday. Bloomberg’s Joumanna Bercetche reports.
title: UAE’s Fujairah Port Hit Again, Oil Loading Suspended

description: European Union foreign ministers are meeting in Brussels today as the conflict in the Middle East continues. NATO's interception of Iranian missiles fired at Turkey and US calls for European nations to help protect oil cargoes in the Strait of Hormuz are set to be top of the agenda. Bloomberg's Oliver Crook reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
